records.functionalSummary: Monolithic ISO 9141 / KWP2000 bidirectional K-Line diagnostic bus transceiver converting 5V MCU UART (RX/TX) to 12V single-wire OBD-II Pin 7 K-Line.

electricalBenchSpecs.supplyVoltage: Pin 7 (VS) = +12V Battery, Pin 3 (VCC) = 5.0V Logic, Pin 5 = GND
keyPinChecks: Pin 6 (K): Bidirectional 12V K-Line to OBD-II Pin 7 (idle ~11V–12V)
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Pin 6 (K-Line) to GND must read high impedance (>10kΩ) unpowered; live idle ~11–12V.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Standard SO-8; check series 510Ω pull-up resistor and protection zener on K-Line.

visualInspectionClues: Burnt K-Line protection diode/resistor next to Pin 6
Cracked SO-8 body
commonFailureModes: Scanner cannot communicate via OBD-II Pin 7 K-Line while engine still runs normally

technicianProTips: On Hitachi MEC11/MEC22 or Bosch ME7 K-Line ECUs, if K-Line idles at 0V instead of ~11.5V, check L9637D Pin 6 for a shorted protection zener or shorted L9637D.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Measure Live K-Line Idle Voltage & Supplies
guidedRepairSteps.action: Check Pin 7 (VS = 12V), Pin 3 (VCC = 5V), and Pin 6 (K-Line idle voltage).
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: VS ≈ 12.6V, VCC = 5.0V, K-Line idle 10.5V–12.2V.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Replace L9637D & Verify 10.4 kbps K-Line Pulses
guidedRepairSteps.action: Swap SO-8 L9637D and verify 0V–12V K-Line diagnostic pulses when scanner initiates handshake.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Clean 0V-to-12V serial frames on Pin 6 and full scanner communication.

records.functionalSummary: High-Speed ISO-11898 CAN protocol transceiver (1 Mbps) with slope-control resistor input (Pin 8 RS) for EMI reduction.

keyPinChecks: Pin 8 RS = GND or slope resistor
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: CANH/CANL to GND >10kΩ unpowered.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Pin-compatible with TJA1050 on 5V boards (verify Pin 8 RS wiring).

visualInspectionClues: Heat spot on SOIC-8 after bus short to +24V/12V
commonFailureModes: Dead CAN bus communication
Excessive 5V rail draw

technicianProTips: Check Pin 8 (RS): if the slope-control resistor to GND is open, MCP2551 stays in standby and will not transmit!

guidedRepairSteps.title: Verify VDD, RS & CAN Bias
guidedRepairSteps.action: Measure Pin 3 (5V), Pin 8 (RS <1V), and Pin 6/7 (~2.5V recessive).
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: 5.0V VDD and balanced 2.5V CAN bias.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Replace MCP2551 & Test Communication
guidedRepairSteps.action: Replace SOIC-8 IC (or upgrade to MCP2561/TJA1050) and verify differential frames.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Clean CAN-H/CAN-L waveform and scanner link.

records.functionalSummary: LIN 2.x / SAE J2602 single-wire 12V transceiver (up to 20 kbps) linking ECU UART to smart alternators, radiator shutters, and body actuators.

electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Pin 6 (LIN) to GND >10kΩ unpowered.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Standard SO-8 rework.

visualInspectionClues: Blown LIN ESD diode near Pin 6
commonFailureModes: Smart alternator charging fault (P0620/U012D)
Cooling fan stuck full-speed or off

technicianProTips: A healthy LIN bus toggles cleanly between ~12V (recessive) and <1.5V (dominant) at 9.6–19.2 kbps. A flat 0V LIN bus usually means a shorted slave (like an alternator regulator) or shorted TJA1020.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Scope Pin 6 (LIN) & Pin 7 (VBAT)
guidedRepairSteps.action: Verify 12V on VBAT and check LIN waveform on oscilloscope.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: 12V recessive idle with crisp 0V–12V data frames.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Replace TJA1020 if Output Driver is Dead
guidedRepairSteps.action: Swap SO-8 transceiver and verify LIN communication restores.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: LIN slave responds cleanly and charging/fan DTC clears.

records.functionalSummary: Industry-standard ISO 11898 High-Speed CAN Transceiver (up to 1 Mbps) bridging the ECU microcontroller CAN controller (TXD/RXD) to the physical CAN-H / CAN-L bus.

keyPinChecks: Pin 8 (S): Silent mode control (0V = Normal mode)
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Unpowered CANH-to-CANL resistance: ~120Ω (if terminal ECU) or >10kΩ (if non-terminal). CANH or CANL shorted to GND/5V (<100Ω) confirms blown transceiver or ESD diode!
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Tiny SO-8 package — easy 350°C hot-air swap; watch nearby 120Ω split termination resistors and common-mode choke.

visualInspectionClues: Cracked or burnt common-mode choke (L1) right next to Pins 6 & 7
Burnt ESD TVS diode (PESD1CAN / NUP2105L) beside CAN pins
Slight bulge or crack on SO-8 TJA1050 body after jump-start surge
commonFailureModes: No OBD-II / CAN communication (U0100) while ECU 5V rail is still healthy
CAN-H or CAN-L stuck at 0V or 5V dragging down the entire vehicle powertrain CAN bus

technicianProTips: Always check the tiny 3-pin CAN ESD protection diode (PESD1CAN / NUP2105L) and the 4-pin common-mode choke BEFORE replacing the TJA1050 — an open choke causes U0100 even when the transceiver is fine!
Confirm Pin 3 (VCC) = 5.0V and Pin 8 (S) = 0V (normal mode) on bench.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Measure Unpowered CAN-H / CAN-L & Choke Continuity
guidedRepairSteps.action: Check CAN-H to CAN-L resistance (expect ~120Ω on terminating ECU) and check both lines to GND and VCC, plus continuity across the CAN common-mode choke.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: No short to GND/VCC; both choke windings <2Ω.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Check Live Recessive Bias & Differential Scope
guidedRepairSteps.action: Power ECU at 12.6V and measure Pin 3 (VCC), Pin 7 (CANH), and Pin 6 (CANL).
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: VCC = 5.0V; Recessive CANH ≈ 2.5V, CANL ≈ 2.5V; Dominant mirrored 3.5V / 1.5V.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Replace TJA1050 (and ESD Diode if Shorted)
guidedRepairSteps.action: Hot-air remove SO-8 TJA1050 at 350°C, verify pad impedance clears, solder replacement TJA1050 (or TJA1051T/3), and re-verify CAN bus frames.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Clean mirrored CAN-H/CAN-L square frames on oscilloscope; scan tool connects.

provenance.liveScrapedSummary: High-Speed CAN Transceiver | NXP Semiconductors — Industry-proven CAN transceiver with standby mode enables reliable automotive networking up to 1 Mbps while reducing power consumption in sleep mode

oemEcuPlatforms: Modern 2015–2026 Toyota / Ford / Nissan / Bosch MED17 / MG1 CAN-FD ECUs
records.functionalSummary: High-Speed CAN / CAN-FD transceiver (up to 5 Mbps in FD) with silent mode and optional Pin 5 VIO (3.3V/5V MCU logic level shifting on /3 variant).

electricalBenchSpecs.supplyVoltage: 5.0V on Pin 3 (VCC); 3.3V or 5.0V on Pin 5 (VIO on TJA1051T/3)
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: CANH/CANL to GND must not be shorted (<100Ω).
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Check variant suffix (/3 has VIO on Pin 5 vs non-/3 N.C.) before swapping with TJA1050!

visualInspectionClues: Burn mark on Pin 6/7 after reverse jump-start or welder surge
commonFailureModes: Bus-off U0073
No ECU communication U0100

technicianProTips: CRITICAL: Do NOT drop a TJA1050 into a 3.3V MCU board that originally used TJA1051T/3 — TJA1050 lacks Pin 5 VIO level shifting and will output 5V into the 3.3V MCU RXD pin!

guidedRepairSteps.title: Confirm Pin 5 (VIO) Voltage
guidedRepairSteps.action: Measure Pin 5 on powered board to verify whether the MCU uses 3.3V VIO logic.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: 3.3V on Pin 5 requires TJA1051T/3 or TJA1042T/3.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Replace Transceiver & Verify CAN-FD Traffic
guidedRepairSteps.action: Swap SO-8 transceiver, inspect common-mode choke, and verify differential waveform.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Clean 2.5V recessive / 3.5V-1.5V dominant differential signals.

provenance.liveScrapedSummary: TJA1051 | High-Speed CAN Transceiver | NXP Semiconductors — NXP

records.functionalSummary: 32-bit Automotive RISC Microcontroller (SuperH / NEC 76F family) powering modern Toyota/Denso gasoline and common-rail diesel ECMs.

keyPinChecks: VCC (5.0V) and Core VDD (1.25V–3.3V) decoupling capacitors
Crystal oscillator (10–20 MHz) active sine wave
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Check 5V VREG and 3.3V rails to GND for shorts before powering.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Denso boards have heavy conformal coating — clean probe tips gently to get accurate readings.

visualInspectionClues: Conformal coating peeling near moisture entry
Corroded vias near connector header
commonFailureModes: P0606 ECM Processor Fault (often triggered by faulty O2 heater short or 5V VREF sag!)

technicianProTips: TOYOTA P0606 PRO TIP: On Toyota/Denso ECUs, P0606 ("ECM Processor") is very frequently triggered by a shorted downstream O2 sensor heater or leaky A/F sensor ground — ALWAYS test O2 sensors before replacing the Denso ECU!

guidedRepairSteps.title: Check Regulated Rails & Conformal Coating Integrity
guidedRepairSteps.action: Verify 5.0V and 3.3V/core rails at MCU decoupling capacitors.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Clean 5.0V and core voltages with no thermal hotspots.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Rule Out External O2 Sensor / 5V VREF Faults
guidedRepairSteps.action: Verify bench ECU boots and communicates cleanly without P0606 when isolated from vehicle O2 harness.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Clean bench OBD-II/CAN communication and stable crystal oscillation.

records.functionalSummary: 32-bit TriCore Automotive Powertrain Microcontroller with integrated Flash, DSP, and multi-channel GPTA timer unit for high-precision injection & ignition.

keyPinChecks: Core VDD (1.3V–1.5V) decoupling caps around MCU perimeter
20.000 MHz Quartz Crystal oscillation (~1Vpp sine wave on XTAL pins)
PORST / Reset pin held HIGH after power stabilization
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Core 1.5V rail naturally reads lower resistance (20Ω–150Ω) than 5V rails; dead short (<2Ω) indicates shorted MLCC decoupling cap or fried MCU core.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: If MCU heats rapidly >70°C at idle (<30s), check decoupling MLCCs around the MCU before condemning the MCU.

visualInspectionClues: Cracked ceramic decoupling capacitor around MCU perimeter
Water-corrosion bridging LQFP-176 pins
commonFailureModes: Dead ECU / no-comm due to missing 1.5V/3.3V rail or dead 20MHz crystal
Internal processor fault P0606

technicianProTips: A "dead" TriCore ECU is 80% of the time a missing 3.3V/1.5V SBC power rail, a shorted ceramic decoupling cap, or a dead 20MHz crystal — ALWAYS check all 3 rails + crystal sine wave before condemning the MCU!

guidedRepairSteps.title: Verify Core (1.3–1.5V), 3.3V, and 5.0V Rails
guidedRepairSteps.action: Measure voltage on decoupling capacitors surrounding the TriCore MCU.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: All 3 rails present and within ±3% with low ripple.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Scope Quartz Crystal & Reset Line
guidedRepairSteps.action: Use 10x oscilloscope probe on crystal pins and verify PORST is HIGH.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Clean 20 MHz sine wave (0.8–1.5Vpp) and stable HIGH reset.

records.functionalSummary: 5A Automotive H-Bridge DC Motor Driver for Electronic Throttle Control (ETC) with short-circuit, overtemperature, and undervoltage shutdown.

electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: OUT1 & OUT2 diode drops to GND and VPWR must be balanced (~0.5V).
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Large exposed bottom pad soldered to GND copper pour.

visualInspectionClues: Blistered HSOP-20 top surface
Burnt copper trace feeding VPWR
commonFailureModes: Throttle limp mode (no pedal response)
SF fault flag permanently pulled low

technicianProTips: Check throttle body motor winding resistance (typically 1.5Ω–4.5Ω) and check for carbon-jammed throttle plates before reinstalling the ECU.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Measure OUT1/OUT2 & SF Pin
guidedRepairSteps.action: Verify OUT1/OUT2 unpowered diode drops and live VPWR voltage.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: VPWR ~12.6V; balanced 0.45–0.65V diode drops on OUT1/OUT2.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Replace MC33186DH & Verify PWM Drive
guidedRepairSteps.action: Preheat PCB, replace HSOP-20 IC, and verify clean complementary PWM output.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Stable motor drive with SF pin released high.

records.functionalSummary: 5A–7A Protected Full H-Bridge DC Motor Driver with SPI diagnostics specifically engineered for Electronic Throttle Control (ETC) and EGR DC motors.

keyPinChecks: VS: Switched +12V battery feed (from Main Relay)
OUT1 & OUT2: Complementary PWM H-bridge motor terminals
DIS / IN / DIR / SPI: 5V control & safety disable lines
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: OUT1 and OUT2 to GND and to VS must read symmetrical body diode drops (~0.50V). Shorted OUT-to-GND or OUT-to-VS locks throttle in limp mode.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Heavy side/bottom heatsink tabs — preheat PCB before desoldering.

visualInspectionClues: Thermal stress browning around Power-SO20
Cracked solder joints on heavy center GND pins
commonFailureModes: Throttle stuck in limp-home position (P2101 / P2119)
Internal H-bridge short blowing ETCS fuse

technicianProTips: Before replacing a TLE7209-2R, verify the ETCS 10A/15A fuse and main relay +12V feed to the VS pin — a blown external ETCS fuse mimics a dead H-bridge IC!

guidedRepairSteps.title: Verify VS (+12V) & VDD (+5V) Feeds
guidedRepairSteps.action: Power bench and confirm +12V on VS and +5V on VDD pins.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Check H-Bridge OUT1/OUT2 Symmetry
guidedRepairSteps.action: Unpowered diode check from OUT1 & OUT2 to GND and VS.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Both motor outputs read matching ~0.45–0.65V drops with no dead shorts.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Rework H-Bridge & Test Throttle Motor Sweep
guidedRepairSteps.action: Replace TLE7209-2R using preheater and confirm complementary PWM on OUT1/OUT2.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Smooth bidirectional PWM drive and zero P2101/P2118 fault codes.

provenance.liveScrapedSummary: BDC motor drivers | Infineon Technologies — MOTIX™ motor control ICs for BDC motors: Explore our portfolio of gate drivers, bridge ICs, and motor system ICs with advanced protection and diagnosi

records.functionalSummary: 500mJ, 360V internally clamped N-Channel EcoSPARK Automotive Ignition IGBT designed to switch primary ignition coils directly from 5V logic gate drive.

electricalBenchSpecs.supplyVoltage: 5V Logic Gate Drive (Pin 1 Gate, Pin 2 Collector/Tab to Coil Primary, Pin 3 Emitter to PGND)
keyPinChecks: Pin 2 (Collector/Tab): Connects to Ignition Coil primary low-side pin
Pin 3 (Emitter): Direct heavy-trace return to Power Ground (PGND)
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Unpowered DMM Resistance: Collector-to-Emitter must read OPEN (>100kΩ) in both directions. Short (<10Ω) confirms blown IGBT.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Collector tab dissipates coil energy; inspect PCB thermal vias and silicone pad under tab.

visualInspectionClues: Pin-hole crater or blister on plastic face of TO-263/TO-220 body
Discolored or lifted Collector copper pad / burnt solder mask
Cracked Emitter shunt resistor (0.02Ω–0.1Ω) next to IGBT
commonFailureModes: Dead Collector-to-Emitter short keeping ignition coil permanently energized (melts coil & blows IGN fuse)
Open Gate drive resistor (100Ω–330Ω) causing dead cylinder misfire

technicianProTips: NEVER install the repaired ECU back onto the vehicle without first testing the external ignition coil primary resistance (typically 0.5Ω–1.2Ω). A shorted coil will instantly destroy the new IGBT.
Always check the small SMD gate drive resistor (100Ω–470Ω) and current-sense shunt resistor beside the failed IGBT.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Unpowered Collector-Emitter Short Check
guidedRepairSteps.action: Measure resistance between Pin 2 (Collector tab) and Pin 3 (Emitter) with ECU unpowered.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Known-Good: >100kΩ (OL). Faulty: <20Ω indicates shorted IGBT.
guidedRepairSteps.safetyNote: Disconnect bench PSU before resistance/diode checks.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Verify Gate Drive Resistor & Pre-Driver
guidedRepairSteps.action: Measure the SMD gate series resistor feeding Pin 1 and compare diode-mode drop on Pin 1 to GND against an adjacent working cylinder IGBT.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Gate-to-GND resistance matches healthy neighbor channel within ±10%.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Hot-Air Desolder & Clean Thermal Pad
guidedRepairSteps.action: Preheat PCB underside to 150°C, use 380°C hot air with flux to lift the failed D2PAK/TO-220 IGBT, wick old solder, and inspect copper pad integrity.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Clean, flat Collector thermal pad with intact vias and zero lifted traces.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Solder Replacement & Verify Bench Dwell
guidedRepairSteps.action: Solder new ISL9V5036P3 (or NGB8201N), clean flux with 99% IPA, power bench at 12.6V with current limit 1.5A, and verify clean 3–4ms dwell pulse on oscilloscope.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: No idle current spike; crisp Collector pull-down to <0.5V during dwell.

provenance.liveScrapedSummary: Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistors - IGBT — onsemi supplies insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs) for electronic ignition, flash, motor drive, and other high current switching applications.

records.functionalSummary: 20A, 350V–400V clamped automotive ignition IGBT with internal gate-emitter ESD zener clamp for harsh inductive coil switching.

electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Unpowered C-E >100kΩ; Gate-to-Emitter internal resistor ~15kΩ–22kΩ.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Use high-thermal-mass soldering iron or preheater to avoid lifting D2PAK tab.

visualInspectionClues: Soot/burn marks near coil driver bank
Melted solder on Emitter pin
commonFailureModes: Shorted C-E locking coil ON
Failed open causing single-cylinder no-spark

technicianProTips: Verify spark plug gap and coil secondary boot insulation on the vehicle — high-voltage flashover backfeeds the IGBT collector and kills replacements.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Isolate Shorted Channel
guidedRepairSteps.action: Measure C-E resistance across every coil IGBT.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Open (>100kΩ) on healthy channels; replace any channel reading <50Ω.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Rework & Bench Oscilloscope Dwell Test
guidedRepairSteps.action: Replace NGB8201N, clean board, and verify clean ignition trigger pulse on bench.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Stable 5V gate pulse and crisp collector ground switching.

provenance.liveScrapedSummary: Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistors - IGBT — onsemi supplies insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs) for electronic ignition, flash, motor drive, and other high current switching applications.

records.functionalSummary: 370V logic-level clamped automotive ignition IGBT with integrated ESD gate-emitter protection and rugged avalanche energy capability.

keyPinChecks: Pin 1 (Gate): 5V logic pulse from ECU ignition pre-driver
Pin 2 (Collector/Tab): Primary coil low-side switch output
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Collector-to-Emitter must be open (>100kΩ) unpowered; Gate-to-Emitter typically 10kΩ–25kΩ.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Requires full solder fillet on D2PAK collector tab for thermal dissipation.

visualInspectionClues: Cracked D2PAK epoxy
Darkened PCB around Collector tab
Open solder joint on Emitter leg
commonFailureModes: Shorted C-E causing blown coil fuse
Intermittent thermal open when engine bay heats up

technicianProTips: Always compare all 4 (or 6) ignition channels in diode mode before powering the bench — a mismatched Gate drop reveals a damaged pre-driver IC.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Compare All Ignition Channels in Diode Mode
guidedRepairSteps.action: Probe Gate-to-GND and Collector-to-GND across all ignition IGBTs with red probe on GND.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: All channels match within ±0.03V; shorted channel reads ~0.00V–0.05V.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Replace IGBT & Verify Coil Primary Resistance
guidedRepairSteps.action: Replace failed STGB10NB37LZ with preheated hot-air rework and confirm vehicle ignition coil resistance is within OEM spec before reinstallation.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: New IGBT reads OL C-E; bench standby current stays normal (<0.35A).

records.functionalSummary: 55V, 42A, 27mΩ logic-level N-Channel Power MOSFET widely used for fuel injectors, SCV/IMV diesel metering valves, VVT solenoids, and heater circuits.

electricalBenchSpecs.supplyVoltage: 5V Logic-Level Gate Drive (Pin 1 Gate, Pin 2 Drain/Tab, Pin 3 Source)
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Body diode (Red on Source, Black on Drain) reads ~0.45V–0.60V; reverse reads OL. Short (<5Ω) = failed MOSFET.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: DPAK tab requires clean thermal solder joint.

visualInspectionClues: Blistered DPAK epoxy
Lifted Source leg solder joint
commonFailureModes: Drain-Source dead short keeping solenoid/injector constantly ON
Gate-Source short loading down MCU/driver

technicianProTips: When replacing an ECU MOSFET, always verify it is a LOGIC-LEVEL (Vgs(th) 1V–2V) MOSFET like IRLR2905 — a standard 10V-gate MOSFET will overheat and fail under 5V ECU gate drive.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Test Body Diode & Gate-Source Resistance
guidedRepairSteps.action: Use DMM diode mode across Drain-Source and resistance across Gate-Source.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Forward body diode 0.45–0.60V, reverse OL, Gate-Source >10kΩ.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Replace Logic-Level MOSFET & Scope PWM
guidedRepairSteps.action: Replace DPAK MOSFET, clean flux, and confirm crisp PWM switching on bench.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Clean Drain switching to <0.2V ON-state with zero thermal runaway.

records.functionalSummary: Smart Power multi-channel engine management actuator driver integrating injector drivers, relay drivers, stepper/idle control, and 5V regulator/watchdog supervision.

keyPinChecks: 5V Regulated output / Reset pin: 5.0V steady, RESET high after boot
Injector & Relay driver pins: Open-drain low-side switches
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Compare diode drop across injector output pins (0.45V–0.65V typical); check VBAT-to-GND for shorts.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: PowerSSO-36 bottom slug is soldered directly to PCB ground plane.

visualInspectionClues: Blistered epoxy on PowerSSO-36 body
Oxidized legs near ECU connector moisture path
commonFailureModes: No fuel pump relay prime
Dead injector bank
Missing 5V / stuck MCU Reset

technicianProTips: Because L9132 integrates multiple powertrain functions, always verify both 5V output and MCU RESET pin before condemning the main CPU.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Verify VBAT, 5V Rail & RESET Line
guidedRepairSteps.action: Power ECU on bench at 12.6V and measure VBAT, 5V supply, and RESET pin.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: VBAT 12.6V, 5V rail 4.95V–5.05V, RESET ~5.0V high.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Diode-Check Outputs & Rework PowerSSO-36
guidedRepairSteps.action: Test all actuator outputs unpowered; if shorted/open, preheat board and replace L9132 with flux and microscope verification.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Balanced diode drops across injector outputs and normal main relay latch.

records.functionalSummary: Automotive engine control IC providing 4 low-side injector/solenoid drivers and 4 ignition IGBT pre-drivers with SPI fault diagnostics.

electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: OUT0–OUT3 diode drop 0.45V–0.65V to GND; GD0–GD3 symmetrical impedance.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Exposed pad must be well soldered to GND.

visualInspectionClues: Heat discoloration near OUT0–OUT3 pins
commonFailureModes: Loss of ignition gate drive to one cylinder after an external IGBT short backfed GDx

technicianProTips: Whenever an ignition IGBT shorts Gate-to-Collector, it can send 12V–300V back into the MC33810 GDx pre-driver pin. Always check GDx impedance!

guidedRepairSteps.title: Check GD0–GD3 Pre-Driver Outputs
guidedRepairSteps.action: Measure diode-mode drop on GD0–GD3 pins to GND and compare all 4 channels.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: All 4 GDx channels read identical voltage drop within ±0.03V.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Replace MC33810 & Verify SPI Comm
guidedRepairSteps.action: Reflow replacement 32-SOICW-EP with preheater and test both injector and ignition gate pulses on bench.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Clean 5V gate pulses on GD0–GD3 and crisp low-side switching on OUT0–OUT3.

records.functionalSummary: 16-channel Smart Power low-side DMOS switch with 16-bit SPI diagnostics and 8 parallel direct inputs for driving fuel injectors, relays, purge valves, and warning lamps.

electricalBenchSpecs.supplyVoltage: 5.0V Logic Supply (VDD) + Exposed Ground Thermal Slug
keyPinChecks: VDD (5V logic rail): Must read 4.9V–5.1V with ignition ON
SPI Bus (SCLK, SI, SO, CS): Active 5V logic bursts during ECU boot
OUT1–OUT16: Open-drain outputs clamping inductive loads at ~45V–60V
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Diode mode (Red on GND, Black on OUTx): healthy DMOS output reads ~0.45V–0.65V body diode drop. <0.05V indicates shorted output MOSFET.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Has a large exposed ground slug underneath — MUST preheat PCB bottom to 160°C before hot-air removal.

visualInspectionClues: Tiny pin-hole burn mark on top package epoxy
Green/white corrosion bridges between fine-pitch 0.65mm pins (water ingress)
Thermal camera shows >85°C hotspot immediately when +12V is applied
commonFailureModes: One or more injector/relay outputs stuck continuously grounded (flooding cylinder or main relay stuck ON)
Internal VDD-to-GND short pulling down the entire ECU 5V regulator rail (no-comm / dead ECU)

technicianProTips: If the ECU 5V rail is shorted to ground, inject 1.0V / 1.0A current-limited onto the 5V rail and inspect with a thermal camera — a shorted TLE6240GP lights up immediately.
Check the fuel injector or purge solenoid coil resistance on the vehicle before returning the ECU; a shorted 1Ω solenoid will re-blow the new channel.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Check 5V Rail & All 16 Output Channels in Diode Mode
guidedRepairSteps.action: With ECU unpowered, probe VDD-to-GND and compare diode-mode voltage on OUT1–OUT16 against GND.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: VDD-to-GND >0.35V diode drop; all OUT channels 0.45V–0.65V.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Preheat & Remove PG-DSO-36 with Hot Air
guidedRepairSteps.action: Use underside PCB preheater (150–165°C) + 390°C hot air with tacky flux to evenly melt the center ground slug and all 36 pins.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Zero lifted fine-pitch pads; intact center ground thermal pad.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Solder New TLE6240GP & Verify Under Microscope
guidedRepairSteps.action: Tin center pad lightly, align Pin 1 dot, reflow until IC self-centers, then touch up all 36 legs with bevel tip and verify zero solder bridges.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Clean shiny fillets on all 36 pins; no adjacent pin shorts.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Bench Power-Up & Actuator Load Test
guidedRepairSteps.action: Power ECU at 12.6V (1A limit), confirm stable 5.0V rail, and verify clean injector/relay switching on oscilloscope.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: 5.0V ±0.1V rail; crisp low-side pulse with clean inductive flyback.

records.functionalSummary: 7-channel 50V / 500mA Darlington transistor array with built-in common-cathode flyback clamping diodes for relays, solenoids, and cluster lamps.

electricalBenchSpecs.supplyVoltage: 5V Logic Inputs (Pins 1–7), Pin 8 = GND, Pin 9 = COM (+12V Flyback Clamp), Pins 10–16 = Outputs
keyPinChecks: Pin 9 (COM): +12V ignition supply for internal flyback clamp diodes
Pins 1–7 -> Pins 16–10: Inverting low-side Darlington drivers
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Pin 10–16 to Pin 9 (COM) reads ~0.55V–0.70V forward clamp diode drop.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: No bottom thermal pad — easy hot-air or iron rework.

visualInspectionClues: Cracked SOIC-16 package
Burnt trace on Pin 8 (GND) or Pin 9 (COM)
commonFailureModes: Relay stuck ON (shorted output channel)
Relay will not energize despite 5V input on Pin 1–7

technicianProTips: Quick live test: if an input pin (1–7) is 5V high, its opposite output pin (16–10) MUST pull down below 1.2V. If it stays at 12V, that Darlington channel is open.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Verify Input vs Opposite Output Voltage
guidedRepairSteps.action: Measure input pin (1–7) and opposite output pin (16–10) with bench powered.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Input >3.5V -> Output <1.2V; Input <0.5V -> Output ~VBAT.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Replace SOIC-16 Array & Verify Relay Load
guidedRepairSteps.action: Swap ULN2003A and confirm external relay coil resistance is >60Ω.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Clean relay pull-in with zero excessive IC heating.

records.functionalSummary: Precision quartz crystal or ceramic resonator generating the master clock frequency for the ECU microcontroller and CAN baud-rate timing.

electricalBenchSpecs.supplyVoltage: 0.8V–2.5Vpp sine wave centered near 1.5V–2.5V on XTAL1/XTAL2
keyPinChecks: Use 10x oscilloscope probe (1x probe capacitance can stall oscillation!)
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Check the two tiny load capacitors (15pF–22pF) beside the crystal for shorts.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Mechanical shock (dropped ECU) frequently fractures the internal quartz wafer.

visualInspectionClues: Dented metal crystal can
Cracked ceramic SMD resonator after impact
commonFailureModes: ECU completely dead (5V rail OK, no CAN/K-Line, zero activity)
Off-frequency clock causing CAN baud mismatch U0100

technicianProTips: ALWAYS switch your oscilloscope probe to 10x attenuation when probing a quartz crystal — a 1x probe adds ~100pF capacitance and can stop a healthy crystal from oscillating!

guidedRepairSteps.title: Probe Crystal Pins with 10x Oscilloscope Probe
guidedRepairSteps.action: Power ECU on bench and probe both crystal pins with 10x scope probe.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Clean, steady sine wave matching stamped MHz frequency (e.g. 16.000 or 20.000 MHz).

guidedRepairSteps.title: Replace Crystal if Flatline (with Healthy 5V/3.3V)
guidedRepairSteps.action: Verify load caps are not shorted, replace crystal with exact MHz automotive-grade part, and re-verify oscillation.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Crisp clock sine wave and immediate ECU wake-up / scanner response.

oemEcuPlatforms: Universal ECU Ignition IGBT & Injector Current-Feedback Stages
records.functionalSummary: Low-value precision metal-strip shunt resistor placed in series with IGBT emitters or injector MOSFET sources so the ECU can measure real-time coil/injector current.

electricalBenchSpecs.supplyVoltage: Millivolt drop proportional to load current (V = I × R)
keyPinChecks: Reads near 0.0Ω–0.2Ω on standard DMM (subtract probe lead resistance)
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: If an R050 (0.05Ω) or R100 (0.10Ω) shunt reads >1Ω or OL, it is blown open!
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Blows open like a fuse when an IGBT or injector driver suffers a catastrophic short.

visualInspectionClues: Crack across wide 2512 resistor body
Charred solder joints
commonFailureModes: No spark / no injector pulse even after replacing the IGBT because the Emitter/Source shunt is open

technicianProTips: NEVER replace a blown 0.05Ω current-sense shunt with a straight wire jumper! Without the exact resistance value, the ECU cannot detect coil saturation or short circuits and will destroy the new IGBT.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Zero DMM Leads & Measure Shunt Resistance
guidedRepairSteps.action: Short DMM probes together to note lead offset, then measure across the 2512 shunt.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Matches printed code (R050 = 0.05Ω, R100 = 0.10Ω) within ±5%.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Replace with Exact Value & Wattage Shunt
guidedRepairSteps.action: Solder exact-value automotive metal-strip shunt resistor and re-verify driver channel.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Normal current feedback and clean coil/injector dwell waveform.

oemEcuPlatforms: Universal 12V Automotive ECUs (located directly beside +B / +12V connector pins)
records.functionalSummary: 600W–1500W Automotive Transient Voltage Suppressor (TVS) diode protecting the ECU +12V power input against reverse polarity, jump-start spikes, and alternator load-dump.

electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Unpowered Diode Mode: ~0.45V–0.65V forward (Red on Anode/GND, Black on Cathode/+12V), OL reverse. A reading of 0.00V–0.05V in BOTH directions confirms a sacrificed shorted TVS diode!
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: When shorted after a reverse-polarity jump start, it intentionally sacrifices itself to blow the main EFI fuse and save the MCU.

visualInspectionClues: Cracked black rectangular SMB/SMC diode right next to the ECU main connector
Soot or burnt copper trace leading from +12V pin to the TVS diode
commonFailureModes: Dead +12V-to-GND short blowing the vehicle EFI/ECM fuse immediately upon key-on

technicianProTips: REVERSE JUMP-START MIRACLE FIX: 70% of ECUs brought in after a reverse-polarity jump start ONLY have a shorted input TVS diode (and possibly one burnt PCB ground trace). Remove the shorted TVS, verify the +12V rail short clears, replace with a new SMBJ18A/SMCJ18A, and repair the fuse trace!

guidedRepairSteps.title: Diode-Check Input TVS Beside Main Connector
guidedRepairSteps.action: Probe both ends of the large SMB/SMC protection diode near the +12V connector pins.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Healthy: ~0.55V one way, OL reverse. Shorted: ~0.00V both ways.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Remove Shorted TVS & Verify Short Clears
guidedRepairSteps.action: Desolder the shorted TVS diode and re-measure +12V-to-GND resistance.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: +12V-to-GND resistance rises from <5Ω to >1kΩ (short cleared!).

guidedRepairSteps.title: Install New TVS Diode & Repair Burnt Trace
guidedRepairSteps.action: Solder new SMBJ18A/SMCJ18A observing cathode stripe orientation, repair any blown copper trace with insulated jumper wire, and power up with 1A current limit.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Normal bench standby draw (0.15A–0.35A) and 5.0V rail restored.

records.functionalSummary: Bulk power-rail decoupling & noise-filtering electrolytic capacitors stabilizing the +12V input and +5V regulated ECU rails.

electricalBenchSpecs.supplyVoltage: Rated 35V–50V on 12V rail; 16V–25V on 5V rail (105°C–125°C Automotive Grade)
keyPinChecks: Check surrounding copper traces for corrosive electrolyte damage
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Must NOT read dead short across terminals; leaking electrolyte creates conductive greenish/brown residue between adjacent traces.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Always replace with 105°C or 125°C low-ESR automotive-grade capacitors — never 85°C consumer caps.

visualInspectionClues: Fishy odor when heated with soldering iron
Dull/oxidized solder joints or dark brown/green crust beneath capacitor base
Bulging top vent or corroded nearby PCB vias
commonFailureModes: Intermittent no-start / random stalling
Corroded open PCB traces under cap causing injector/idle/5V failures

technicianProTips: CLASSIC TOYOTA & MITSUBISHI ECU FIX: Even if an old capacitor looks fine from above, electrolyte leaks underneath and eats through the copper traces! Always wash the area thoroughly with isopropyl alcohol + brush and continuity-test every via under the cap.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Inspect Base for Electrolyte Crust & Measure ESR
guidedRepairSteps.action: Inspect under magnification for dull joints/residue and test capacitance/ESR.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Zero leakage; ESR <1Ω and capacitance within ±20%.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Remove, Neutralize & Continuity-Test Hidden Traces
guidedRepairSteps.action: Desolder aged caps, scrub board cleanly with 99% IPA, and beep-test every trace/via underneath.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Clean bright copper pads; jump any eaten traces with enameled wire.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Install 105°C Low-ESR Replacements (Verify Polarity)
guidedRepairSteps.action: Solder new 105°C/125°C automotive capacitors observing exact +/- polarity.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Ripple <25mV on 5V rail; ECU boots cleanly.

records.functionalSummary: Microwire 3-wire Serial EEPROM (2Kbit–16Kbit) universally used in Japanese Denso/Keihin ECUs and immobilizer boxes for key/VIN/trim storage.

electricalBenchSpecs.supplyVoltage: Pin 8 (VCC) = 5.0V (or 3.3V), Pin 5 (VSS) = GND (NOTE: Pin 5 is GND, NOT Pin 4!)
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Pin 8 (VCC) to Pin 5 (GND) >0.40V diode mode.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Watch for rotated pinout variants (e.g. Rohm BR93L56RF-W vs standard)!

visualInspectionClues: Tiny TSSOP-8/MSOP-8 labeled RH56 / RA57 / L56R near main Denso MCU
commonFailureModes: Immobilizer mismatch (B2799 on Toyota)
Corrupted learned idle/fuel trim memory

technicianProTips: Toyota Denso ECUs often mark 93C56 as "RH56", "RA57", or "L56R". Remember Pin 5 is GND on Microwire 93Cxx (whereas Pin 4 is GND on SPI 95xxx and I2C 24Cxx)!

guidedRepairSteps.title: Confirm Package Marking & Pin 5 GND Orientation
guidedRepairSteps.action: Identify exact marking (RH56/RA57/93C66) and verify Pin 5 continuity to board GND.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Pin 5 = 0Ω to GND; Pin 8 = 5.0V (or 3.3V) when powered.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Verify Boot Clock/Data Activity
guidedRepairSteps.action: Probe Pin 2 (CLK) and Pin 4 (DO) with oscilloscope at ignition ON.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Short digital burst on CLK/DO within 100ms of ECU wake-up.

records.functionalSummary: 16-Kbit (2KB) Automotive SPI Serial EEPROM storing VIN, immobilizer keys, injector trim codes, and adaptive fault memory.

keyPinChecks: Pin 1 (/S Chip Select), Pin 2 (Q Data Out), Pin 5 (D Data In), Pin 6 (C Clock)
Pin 3 (/W Write Protect) & Pin 7 (/HOLD): Normally tied HIGH to VCC
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Pin 8 to Pin 4 >0.40V diode mode; verify continuity of SPI traces to MCU.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Keep hot-air temperature <=330°C and brief duration (<15s) to prevent thermal data retention loss!

visualInspectionClues: Prior sloppy rework flux or lifted Pin 1/Pin 8 pad
Missing tiny 0402 pull-up resistor on /CS
commonFailureModes: Corrupted EEPROM checksum (P0601/P0602/P0603)
Immobilizer no-start after battery cranking voltage drop

technicianProTips: ALWAYS take a verified read backup of the EEPROM BEFORE any hot-air rework near it, and never exceed 330°C on SO-8 EEPROMs.
NOTE: AutoElectric Lab Pro is a virtual diagnostic/repair learning lab — physical EEPROM reading/programming requires dedicated bench programmer hardware and OEM authorization.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Verify VCC, GND & /HOLD /WP Pins
guidedRepairSteps.action: Check Pin 8 (3.3V/5V), Pin 4 (0V), and confirm Pin 3 & Pin 7 are high on powered bench.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Stable 3.3V or 5.0V VCC with zero rail dropout.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Inspect SPI Pins & Solder Joints Under Microscope
guidedRepairSteps.action: Inspect Pins 1, 2, 5, 6 for cold joints or corroded vias; reflow gently with iron if cracked.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Clean SPI clock/data burst visible on oscilloscope during ECU ignition-ON boot.

records.functionalSummary: 1A, 26V Automotive Low-Dropout (0.5V dropout) 5.0V Voltage Regulator with reverse-battery and load-dump transient protection.

electricalBenchSpecs.supplyVoltage: Pin 1 = IN (6.5V–26V), Pin 2/Tab = GND, Pin 3 = OUT (5.0V)
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Pin 3 (5V) to GND >0.35V diode mode; requires >=22µF output capacitor for stability.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: Requires >=22µF low-ESR output capacitor or the 5V rail will oscillate!

visualInspectionClues: Overheated SOT-223 tab
Dry/leaking 22µF output capacitor
commonFailureModes: Oscillating 5V rail causing random ECU resets
Zero 5V output

technicianProTips: LM2940 MUST have at least a 22µF output capacitor with proper ESR (0.1Ω–1Ω); a dried-out electrolytic cap causes high-frequency oscillation on the 5V rail that crashes the MCU.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Scope 5V Output for Ripple / Oscillation
guidedRepairSteps.action: Connect oscilloscope AC-coupled on Pin 3 (5V OUT).
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: DC 5.0V with <30mV peak-to-peak ripple.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Replace LM2940 & 22µF Output Cap
guidedRepairSteps.action: Replace regulator and output capacitor if voltage sags or oscillates.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Clean 5.0V output under load.

records.functionalSummary: 450mA Automotive 5.0V Low-Dropout (LDO) Voltage Regulator with integrated Power-On Reset (RO) and 42V load-dump protection.

electricalBenchSpecs.supplyVoltage: Pin 1 (I) = 12V Input, Pin 3 (GND/Tab) = GND, Pin 5 (Q) = 5.0V ±2% Output
keyPinChecks: Pin 2 (RO Reset Output): ~5.0V high when rail is healthy
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Pin 5 (5V out) to GND must read >0.35V in diode mode; <0.05V means downstream 5V short!
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: If TLE4275G is scorching hot (>90°C), check for a shorted external 5V sensor or shorted tantalum/ceramic cap on the 5V rail BEFORE replacing the regulator.

visualInspectionClues: Blistered 5-pin D2PAK
Cracked/burnt input or output SMD electrolytic/tantalum capacitor
commonFailureModes: Dead ECU (0V on 5V rail)
Sensor 5V reference drop (P0641 / P0651)
Continuous MCU reset loop

technicianProTips: A hot 5V LDO regulator is often a VICTIM, not the culprit! Unpowered, check Pin 5 (5V) to GND — if shorted, remove shorted filter caps or trace the 5V bus before replacing the TLE4275G.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Check 5V Output Rail for Downstream Short
guidedRepairSteps.action: Measure resistance/diode drop from Pin 5 (Q) to Pin 3 (GND) unpowered.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: >300Ω / >0.35V diode drop. Clear any downstream 5V short first.

guidedRepairSteps.title: Verify Input Voltage (Pin 1) & Output (Pin 5)
guidedRepairSteps.action: Apply 12.6V bench power and measure Pin 1, Pin 5, and Pin 2 (Reset).

guidedRepairSteps.title: Replace Regulator & Output Filter Capacitors
guidedRepairSteps.action: Preheat PCB, replace TLE4275G, and inspect/replace aged 22µF–100µF output caps.
guidedRepairSteps.targetSpec: Rock-solid 5.00V rail with <20mV ripple on oscilloscope.

keyPinChecks: V5V / T5V1 / T5V2: 5.0V ±2% (tracker supplies for TPS/MAP/CKP)
MR (Main Relay Driver): Pulls low when IGN wake-up is active
electricalBenchSpecs.diodeOrResistanceCheck: Check T5V1, T5V2, and V5V rails to GND in diode mode before powering.
electricalBenchSpecs.thermalNote: 100-pin LQFP with bottom ground slug — requires precision preheater + hot air and microscope inspection.

visualInspectionClues: Corrosion along LQFP-100 perimeter pins
Hotspot on SBC die during 5V rail fault
commonFailureModes: Missing 5V tracker output (P0641/P0651)
ECU fails to wake up on IGN switch

guidedRepairSteps.title: Precision LQFP-100 Rework
guidedRepairSteps.action: Preheat PCB to 160°C, replace TLE8888QK, inspect all 100 pins under magnification, and clean thoroughly.
